models_evaluated: three other machine learning models for surgery recommendation

links.outcome: Fairness metrics and model performance with vs without race/ethnicity as predictor
links.effect: Excluding race/ethnicity as a predictor in survival and surgery recommendation models improved fairness metrics without degrading model performance; but disparate impact persisted in survival models.
links.quote: The exclusion of race/ethnicity as a predictor in the survival and surgery recommendation models improved fairness metrics without degrading model performance.

links.outcome: Effect of stratified oversampling mitigation on disparate impact and model accuracy
links.effect: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.
links.quote: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.

links.outcome: Fairness metrics across racial/ethnic subgroups for survival and surgery recommendation models
links.effect: Survival models show disparate impact toward non-Hispanic Black patients regardless of whether race/ethnicity was used as a predictor; models including race/ethnicity amplified disparities in the data.
links.quote: The survival models show disparate impact towards non-Hispanic Black patients regardless of whether race/ethnicity is used as a predictor.

links.outcome: Bias in models trained on registry data reflecting real-world disparities
links.effect: Machine learning models amplified racial/ethnic disparities reflected in the data; Black patients less often recommended surgery than White patients even accounting for age and stage.
links.quote: Machine learning models amplified the racial/ethnic disparities across the cancer care continuum (which are reflected in the data used to make model decisions).

links.effect: Including race/ethnicity amplified disparities; excluding it improved fairness metrics without degrading performance.
links.quote: The models including race/ethnicity amplified the disparities observed in the data.

links.effect: Survival models showed disparate impact toward non-Hispanic Black patients, with or without race/ethnicity.
links.quote: The survival models show disparate impact towards non-Hispanic Black patients regardless of whether race/ethnicity is used as a predictor.

links.effect: Stratified oversampling reduced disparate impact while reducing model accuracy.
links.quote: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.

links.outcome: disparity amplification from including race or ethnicity as predictor
links.effect: Models including race/ethnicity amplified observed disparities, while survival models showed disparate impact toward non-Hispanic Black patients regardless of whether race/ethnicity was used as a predictor.
links.quote: The models including race/ethnicity amplified the disparities observed in the data.

links.outcome: effect of stratified oversampling on disparate impact and accuracy
links.effect: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.
links.quote: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.
